topic: Classify every nonzero nonconstant homogeneous polynomial denominator D on Sym₃ satisfying 2 tr((G_D(Σ)Σ)^2)=cD(Σ)^2 for c>0. Prove, without degree or nonresonance restrictions, that D is a scalar product of nonnegative integer powers of determinants along one nested rational flag, by establishing global kernel-line constancy for the mixed rank-two branch through adjugate-translation rigidity and cone monotonicity. Give an exact rational-coefficient recognition, exponent, and flag-recovery certificate. Credit Tamano's flag sufficiency, Sym₂ converse, spectral reduction, and determinant stripping. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Differentiating det G=0 in its adjugate direction and using Hessian symmetry gives dG[adj G]=0. The resulting polynomial derivation annihilates G, adj G, and the mixed residue E, so finite Taylor expansion makes E constant on each adjugate ray. Positive-semidefinite gradients, homogeneity, and Loewner ordering then bound every parallel polynomial ray above and below, forcing one fixed global kernel and closing Tamano's remaining mixed branch. Exact symbolic checks passed for flag powers, determinant stripping, a nonnested failure, rational flag recovery, and the resonant deformation Eε=x³(xy-u²)³+ε det(X)x⁶, whose residual is exactly 12ε²x¹²det(X)². UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: The informal universal proof still needs independent verification of the finite adjugate-translation step, its symmetric-coordinate conventions, the two-sided cone-order bound, and every imported reduction from Tamano. Software integration and finite-sample inference are not established. EARLY KILL TEST: Recompute dG[adj G] with half-weighted off-diagonal gradients, then seek a homogeneous polynomial with positive-semidefinite rank-two gradient and moving kernel; either a missing derivative term or such a counterexample kills the spine. open_problems.open_problem: Does every determinant-free mixed-branch solution on Sym₃ have a globally constant kernel line, and hence equal a product of powers of one nested line minor and plane minor?

source_refs.claim: The unrestricted Sym₃ converse is reduced to constancy of the mixed-branch kernel line, requiring more than ordinary vanishing-Hessian arguments.
source_refs.author: Shu Tamano

source_refs.claim: Vanishing-Hessian forms in six variables need not be cones, so Hessian degeneracy alone cannot force a fixed kernel direction.
source_refs.author: Ciro Ciliberto, Francesco Russo, and Aron Simis

source_refs.claim: Cubic vanishing-Hessian classifications exhibit noncone scroll and Perazzo geometries that realize moving polar-map behavior.
source_refs.author: Rodrigo Gondim and Francesco Russo
source_refs.venue: Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra

open_problems.why_unsolved: Tamano reduces the unresolved determinant-free Sym₃ case to a rank-two symmetric relative gradient with fixed spectrum and a polynomially varying kernel line, but the available cofactor syzygies and face restrictions do not glue those directions globally. Classical vanishing-Hessian theory cannot close this step because noncone forms with moving polar geometry exist in the same ambient dimension. The proposed adjugate-translation argument therefore still needs an independently checked symmetric-coordinate identity dG[adj G]=0 and a rigorous two-sided Loewner-order bound showing that positivity, homogeneity, and integrability exclude every moving-kernel geometry.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A degree-unrestricted rigidity theorem proving that Σ ↦ ker G_D(Σ) is constant on the mixed rank-two branch, or an explicit homogeneous positive-cone counterexample with a nonconstant kernel map and a precise statement of which adjugate-translation or cone-order step fails.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation, branch reduction, and statement of the mixed-kernel obstruction directly frame the destination question.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Rational causal estimators have polynomial covariance denominators -> some denominators have noise exactly proportional to magnitude -> flag powers explain the phenomenon and Sym₂ has a converse -> the remaining Sym₃ question is whether the mixed-branch kernel line must be globally constant

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze the polar map and its fibers for a vanishing-Hessian form, distinguishing fixed-vertex cones from noncone developable geometries through the polar image and dual variety.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The mixed-branch kernel line is an infinitesimal fiber direction of a gradient map; this machinery identifies the moving-kernel alternatives that cone positivity and the self-normalization PDE must eliminate.

method_exemplars.technique: Use Bartlett decomposition to factor a recovered flag denominator into independent scaled chi-squares, followed by boundary-sequence studentization and Fieller inversion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once kernel constancy supplies the flag factorization, this converts the classification into an exact pivot and a limit theory for weak denominators.

open_problems.open_problem: Can arbitrary-degree rational-coefficient polynomials on Sym₃ be recognized exactly as self-normalizing flag powers, with a checkable certificate recovering the determinant exponent, integer line and plane exponents, and a nested rational flag?

source_refs.claim: The existing exact factor-and-rank diagnostic is inconclusive when a determinant-free irreducible factor has degree at least three.
source_refs.author: Shu Tamano

source_refs.claim: Gröbner-basis calculations can certify or refute algebraic causal-identification formulas but do not classify denominator self-normalization or recover nested flags.
source_refs.author: Luis David García-Puente, Sarah Spielvogel, and Seth Sullivant

source_refs.excerpt: use adjugates to form the rational entries ... expand each N_k ... and test its finitely many exact coefficients
Dividing numerator and denominator by their greatest common divisor ... gives a unique rational certificate

open_problems.why_unsolved: Coefficient comparison can decide the trace identity after expansion, but it neither discovers the unknown determinant factorization nor certifies that recovered factors arise from one rational nested flag. Tamano's present recovery route handles linear and adjugate-linear factors after determinant stripping, leaving higher-degree irreducibles tied to the unresolved mixed branch. The prior CausalSmith constructions supply denominator clearing, adjugate identities, fraction-free rational kernels, and canonical minor certificates only after the relevant rational maps or linear systems are known. The first new step is a complete factor-or-rigidity procedure that recovers rational flag subspaces and multiplicities without assuming the factor degrees.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sound-and-complete finite algorithm over ℚ whose acceptance certificate contains rational flag generators, nonnegative integer exponents, a scalar, the induced value of c, and exact polynomial-identity receipts, and whose rejection certificate identifies a nonzero residual coefficient or a factor incompatible with any nested rational flag.

writing_exemplar.why: It presents symbolic algebra as a source of independently checkable causal-identification certificates, the appropriate framing for an exact denominator audit.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Graphical models yield rational causal formulas -> exact elimination can certify those formulas -> their denominators require an additional audit of inferential behavior -> recovering exponents and a rational nested flag makes that audit certificate-producing

method_exemplars.technique: Encode covariance relations as polynomial ideals and use exact Gröbner reduction and elimination to return checkable rational-identification or obstruction witnesses.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired recognizer likewise begins with rational polynomial coefficients and must return a symbolic witness checkable without numerical factorization.

method_exemplars.technique: Use fraction-free elimination and Sylvester-identity divisibility to compute rational kernel bases and exact minor certificates while controlling intermediate integer growth.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Rational flag recovery reduces to certified kernel and containment computations for rational symmetric matrices.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate recovered line, plane, and determinant multiplicities into the trace constant and the exact Wishart/Bartlett product pivot.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It specifies the inferential metadata that a successful algebraic recognition certificate must determine.

open_problems.open_problem: For d≥4, does exact self-normalization force one common invariant complete flag for the relative gradients, or can a homogeneous polynomial solution have genuinely varying spectral data and no global recursive ordering?

source_refs.claim: An all-dimensional converse holds conditional on a fixed invariant flag, but exact self-normalization is not known to create that flag for d≥4 because two spectral power sums no longer discretize the spectrum.
source_refs.author: Shu Tamano

source_refs.claim: Recursive triangular structure and basic relative invariants produce nested block coordinates for homogeneous matrix cones, but do not classify self-normalizing polynomials.
source_refs.author: Levent Tunçel and Lieven Vandenberghe

open_problems.why_unsolved: In Sym₃, homogeneity, the trace-square identity, and an additional integral relation reduce the relative-gradient spectrum to finitely many possibilities. For d≥4 the same power-sum constraints leave a positive-dimensional spectral locus, so connectedness no longer forces spectral constancy. Tamano can integrate a fixed invariant ordering into flag powers, while homogeneous-cone theory obtains recursive flags only after assuming substantial automorphism-group structure. No known step derives that ordering solely from the self-normalization PDE.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An all-dimensional sufficient-condition theorem deriving a common invariant complete flag and constant quotient weights from the self-normalization identity, or a smallest-dimensional explicit polynomial counterexample with varying relative-gradient spectrum and a proof that it is not a flag power.

writing_exemplar.why: Its higher-dimensional discussion separates the missing invariant-flag step from the already-solved integration step.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Flag powers self-normalize in every dimension -> Sym₃ spectral finiteness supports a low-dimensional converse -> in d≥4 two power sums permit continuously varying spectra -> determine whether the PDE nevertheless creates a common invariant ordering

method_exemplars.technique: Use triangular automorphism groups, recursive cone decompositions, and basic relative invariants to expose nested coordinates in which logarithmic determinant barriers separate.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Tamano's conditional converse integrates once an invariant ordering exists; homogeneous-cone machinery supplies the closest structural mechanism for producing such an ordering.

method_exemplars.technique: Convert fixed quotient weights into integer determinant exponents and apply independent Bartlett factors to obtain the exact sampling pivot.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the estimation-and-inference rung unlocked if the missing higher-dimensional invariant flag is established.

open_problems.open_problem: Which homogeneous covariance-polynomial denominators remain proportionally self-normalizing under semiparametric sampling families with unrestricted fourth cumulants when variance is computed by the matched sandwich operator?

source_refs.claim: Ellipticity only rescales the Gaussian identity, whereas unrestricted fourth cumulants introduce an additional direction-dependent contraction.
source_refs.author: Shu Tamano

source_refs.claim: Elliptical covariance-structure theory preserves normal-theory asymptotics after a kurtosis adjustment but does not cover unrestricted fourth-cumulant tensors.
source_refs.author: Alexander Shapiro and Michael W. Browne
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Smooth functions of sample covariance matrices have explicit asymptotic variance and higher-order expectation formulas under elliptical laws.
source_refs.author: Toshiya Iwashita and Minoru Siotani

open_problems.why_unsolved: For elliptical laws, the fourth-cumulant contribution collapses to a kurtosis multiple of the Gaussian trace form plus an Euler term, leaving the polynomial class unchanged. With unrestricted fourth cumulants, the additional contraction of ∇D with the cumulant tensor depends on directions not controlled by homogeneity or tr((G_DΣ)^2); even flag denominators therefore need not have sandwich variance proportional to D² throughout the model. The missing ingredient is a specified cumulant class whose tensor geometry is restrictive enough to classify yet broader than ellipticity.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient characterization, for an explicitly stated semiparametric fourth-cumulant class, of pairs (D,𝒫) satisfying ∇D(Σ)ᵀΓ_P(Σ)∇D(Σ)=c_P D(Σ)², together with a consistent matched-sandwich estimator and a uniform limit or coverage theorem for the associated causal ratio estimator.

writing_exemplar.why: It distinguishes algebraic denominator constancy from distribution-specific variance calibration and identifies unrestricted fourth cumulants as the next boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Gaussian covariance noise yields a trace-square identity -> elliptical noise preserves it after one kurtosis correction -> general fourth cumulants introduce direction-specific variance -> characterize when a matched sandwich studentizer still self-normalizes a causal denominator

method_exemplars.technique: Decompose the asymptotic covariance of sample covariances into normal-theory and kurtosis components and prove which scale-invariant functionals retain corrected limit laws.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired theorem must generalize this covariance-operator decomposition from a one-parameter elliptical structure to a stated tensor class.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply higher-order delta expansions to smooth functions of sample covariance matrices with explicit asymptotic variances and second-order expectation terms.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A sandwich-calibrated denominator theorem needs both the first-order cumulant contraction and control of regimes where that contraction degenerates.

open_problems.open_problem: How can inference remain uniformly valid after selecting among multiple rational causal certificates using their observed denominator-strength diagnostics, when candidates may occupy strong, first-order weak, and exactly self-normalizing regimes?

source_refs.claim: Choosing the certificate with the largest observed diagnostic creates a data-adaptive weak-direction problem requiring selection adjustment and simultaneous robust inversion.
source_refs.author: Shu Tamano

source_refs.claim: Debiased estimation with many weak moments accommodates growing nuisance parameters but not post-selection among algebraically distinct rational certificates.
source_refs.author: Rui Wang, Kwun Chuen Gary Chan, and Ting Ye

open_problems.why_unsolved: Each fixed certificate may admit exact flag-power calibration or Fieller-style inversion, but maximizing an estimated strength diagnostic changes the selected denominator's law and couples the numerator, denominator, and selection event. Existing many-weak-moment results handle growing collections of moments and nuisance estimation rather than a menu whose members can lie in qualitatively different algebraic boundary regimes.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A simultaneous or selective confidence-set construction for a finite or growing family {(N_j,D_j)} with uniform 1−α coverage for the common causal target across strong, first-order weak, and exactly self-normalizing sequences, plus a limit theorem for the selected diagnostic and a rule combining bounded and unbounded inversions.

writing_exemplar.why: It makes denominator class a practical choice among equivalent causal certificates and isolates the inferential danger of choosing after observing strength.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: One causal target may have multiple rational certificates -> their denominators can have different weak-limit classes -> practitioners choose the apparently strongest observed certificate -> validity requires inference accounting for certificate selection

method_exemplars.technique: Construct a Neyman-orthogonal debiased estimator and prove asymptotic normality under a growing many-weak-moment regime with nuisance estimation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The selected-certificate problem likewise needs a joint approximation over growing weak directions before maxima or simultaneous inversions can be calibrated.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate primary and debiasing nuisances by penalized minimax criteria and prove root-n inference for a strongly identified functional despite weak nuisance identification.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its proof pattern separates identification strength of the causal target from weakness of an intermediate certificate or nuisance direction.

literature_map:
Tamano (2026, arXiv:2608.20223) introduces exact self-normalization for homogeneous covariance-polynomial denominators and proves flag-power sufficiency in every dimension.
Tamano's Bartlett argument gives a product of independent chi-squares for nested covariance minors, turning the algebraic flag into an exact Gaussian pivot.
The same paper proves the Sym₂ converse and reduces Sym₃ to rank-one, pure plane-minor, and mixed rank-two branches after determinant stripping.
Its principal live gap is the mixed branch: fixed relative spectrum and a polynomial kernel line are known, but global constancy of that line is not.
Ciliberto–Russo–Simis (2008, Advances in Mathematics, arXiv:math/0701596) shows why vanishing Hessian alone is inadequate through noncone vanishing-Hessian geometries.
Gondim–Russo (2015, Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra, arXiv:1312.1618) classifies low-dimensional cubic vanishing-Hessian hypersurfaces via scroll and Perazzo geometry.
Faraut–Korányi (1994) supplies the generalized-power-function language on symmetric cones; Tamano's flag powers specialize it to covariance cones.
Tunçel–Vandenberghe (2022, arXiv:2211.00761) develops triangular recursive structure and relative invariants for homogeneous matrix cones, an adjacent mechanism for invariant-flag extraction in d≥4.
García-Puente–Spielvogel–Sullivant (2010, UAI, arXiv:1007.3784) and Foygel–Draisma–Drton (2012, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1107.5552) give exact or combinatorial pipelines for rational causal certificates but do not classify denominator self-normalization.
Shapiro–Browne (1987, JASA) and Iwashita–Siotani (1994, Canadian Journal of Statistics) show that elliptical covariance-functional inference reduces to kurtosis-adjusted Gaussian structure.
Tamano shows that this elliptical adjustment preserves the algebraic class, while unrestricted fourth-cumulant sandwich self-normalization remains uncharacterized.
Fieller (1954), Dufour (1997), Andrews–Cheng (2012), and Lee–McCrary–Moreira–Porter (2022) anchor weak-denominator inversion and uniform-in-strength inference.
Wang–Chan–Ye (2025, arXiv:2505.07295) treats many weak moments, while Bennett et al. (2026, JRSSB; arXiv:2208.08291) separates strong target functionals from weak nuisance identification.
The remaining inferential tension is that selecting among algebraically distinct rational certificates by observed strength invalidates fixed-certificate calibration.
